fields.notes:
A devotee of Lord Caitanya, a Kāyastha of north Rāḍha and the eldest brother of Vāsudeva Ghoṣa. He led a family life; his descendants belong to the royal family of Dinājpur.

The record also held Kaṁsāri Miśra (cousin of Lord Gaurāṅga) and Kaṁsāri Sena (of Nityānanda's branch), now in records of their own (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Rasamaya Dāsa (attendant of Rasikānanda)
fields.notes:
The domestic attendant of Rasikānanda Prabhu and the father of Gopījanavallabha, the author of the Rasikamaṅgala (Rasikamaṅgala 4.34); the son of the daughter of Bhīma, the zamindar of Dhāreṇḍā. Three poems of «Rasamaya Dāsa» are in the Padakalpataru (which Rasamaya is not known).

The record also held the Rasamaya Dāsa who translated the Gīta-govinda, the author of the Kṛṣṇa-bhakti-vallī, and Viṣṇudāsa the disciple of Śyāmānanda, called Rasamaya, now in records of their own (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Vasanta Rāya (of Jessore)
fields.notes:
A Kāyastha, the son of Guṇānanda Guhā and the cousin of Pratāpāditya, the king of Bengal; with his cousin Vikramāditya he founded the kingdom of Jessore. Around 1570, with his help, Guṇānanda built a new temple south of the old temple of Madanamohana in Vṛndāvana (see «Guṇānanda Guhā»).

The record also held the Vasanta Rāya disciple of Narottama Ṭhākura, the poet, now in records of their own (07-11-2026).
Taken out of the record «Vasanta Rāya» #1647, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).
